questions.prompt: You hit a failure you do not understand. Walk through U02's debugging method before touching the code: what do you establish first, and how do you shrink the problem?

keyPoints.text: First pin down exactly what you expected versus what you observed
keyPoints.quote: Start with a precise difference between expected and observed behavior.

keyPoints.text: Shrink the input until the failure is small enough to reason about
keyPoints.quote: Reduce the input until the failure is easy to reason about.

keyPoints.text: An experiment must be able to tell competing causes apart, not just confirm one
keyPoints.quote: A hypothesis proposes a cause; an experiment should distinguish it from another cause.

keyPoints.text: Look at values right at the boundary and vary a single thing per step
keyPoints.quote: Inspect values at a boundary and change one thing at a time.

keyPoints.text: A minimal reproduction keeps the failure while unrelated code goes away
keyPoints.quote: A minimal reproduction preserves the failure while removing unrelated code.

keyPoints.text: Breakpoints or targeted logs probe a hypothesis, and the debug noise comes out afterward
keyPoints.quote: Use a breakpoint or targeted log to inspect a hypothesis; remove debug noise afterward.

questions.prompt: Classify the three kinds of errors U02 names and trace the worked loop example: why is the printed total NaN, and what must the regression test guarantee?

keyPoints.text: Syntax stops parsing, runtime interrupts execution, and logic quietly yields plausible wrong answers
keyPoints.quote: Syntax errors prevent parsing, runtime errors interrupt execution and logic errors can produce plausible wrong answers.

keyPoints.text: In the worked example only indices 0 through 2 exist, so the loop's read of index 3 gives undefined
keyPoints.quote: Indices 0, 1 and 2 exist; index 3 is undefined.

keyPoints.text: Checking i and samples[i] separates a boundary mistake from bad data
keyPoints.quote: Inspect i and samples[i] to distinguish a boundary error from invalid data.

keyPoints.text: Rewriting the expectation to match the bug would hide the defect, not fix it
keyPoints.quote: Changing the expected answer would conceal the defect.

keyPoints.text: The regression has to fail on the old defect and pass once corrected
keyPoints.quote: A regression must fail under the old defect and pass after the correction.

keyPoints.text: Off-by-one, accidental mutation and string/number mix-ups each deserve their own experiment
keyPoints.quote: Off-by-one errors, accidental mutation and string/number confusion deserve explicit experiments.

questions.prompt: State the findTitles repair contract and its delayed transfer: what must the search do, and how do you approach a search that fails only at the last item?

keyPoints.text: The search matches a trimmed, case-insensitive substring of each title
When the query is only whitespace, every title comes back
keyPoints.quote: A whitespace-only query returns all titles.

keyPoints.text: Title text, result order and the input array all stay intact
keyPoints.quote: Preserve title text, order and input.

keyPoints.text: The transfer scenario is a search that only misses the final item
keyPoints.quote: A search fails only at the last item.

keyPoints.text: Before editing, name two candidate causes and an experiment that separates them
keyPoints.quote: Propose two different causes and an experiment separating them before editing.

keyPoints.text: Come back days and then weeks later with the earlier solution closed
keyPoints.quote: Revisit after 2–7 days and around three weeks with the prior solution closed.
